newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco's stock market ends nearly unchanged.
newsitem.headline: Morocco's stock market ends nearly unchanged.

text.p: The Casablanca stock exchange closed on Tuesday 0.26 percent higher with the main trading being in Samir oil refinery, Wafabank and Societe Nationale d'Investissement, a market analyst said.
The all-share index closed at 682.86 points from 681.12 points on Monday.
"The same characteristics still shape the market, with few stocks available and a lot of money on the market notably through mutual funds," a Casablanca-based broker said.
Samir fell 8.95 dirhams to 317 dirhams with 11,191 shares traded.
In the banking sector, the biggest rise was in Banque Marocaine du Commerce Exterieur, one of the market blue chips. Its shares rose 19 dirhams to close at 666 dirhams.
Wafabank remained unchanged at 860 dirhams with 5,245 shares traded.

Steel mill Sonasid, one of the four stocks to be traded electronically, fell 17 dirhams to 567 dirhams with 354 shares exchanged. Six other stocks are to be introduced on the new system in the next two months, the broker said.
Societe Nationale d'Investissement, Morocco's second largest conglomerate which holds diversified stakes in more than 40 firms, gained 10 dirhams to close at 790 dirhams with 5,949 shares traded.
ONA group, Morocco's largest private holding, shed one dirham to close at 830 dirhams with 4,882 shares changing hands.
Leasing firm, Maroc Leasing lost 13 dirhams for a second consecutive day, closing at 421 dirhams.
In the agro-industry sector, dairy firm Centrale Laitiere jumped 124 dirhams to 3,090 dirhams with only 75 shares traded. Edible oil firm Lesieur took 35 dirhams to 2,500 dirhams.
Brewery company Brasseries du Maroc rose 56 dirhams to 1,931 dirhams with 727 shares exchanged.
"The agro-industry sector is thriving but the increase in prices is also because there is a shortage of stocks," the stockbroker said.
Total volume traded was 81 million dirhams. It was divided into 68.5 million dirhams in share trading and 3.6 million dirhams in privatisation bonds on the official market, a broker said.
The remaining 8.9 million dirhams was traded on the over the counter market, he said, attributing its low turnover to more caution on the part of shareholders.
